Repeated tuning on a small fixed validation cohort can overfit the validation feedback. [Dwork et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629) formalize this problem and propose protected holdout reuse; their guarantees require an evaluation mechanism beyond ordinary score reporting. For this pinned benchmark, practical safeguards are to predeclare search spaces, evaluation frequency and stopping rules; log every attempted configuration; limit adaptive comparisons; and reserve hidden evaluation for the final selection. These safeguards reduce selection pressure but do not eliminate adaptive bias.

For paired HR@10 uncertainty, retain each user’s binary hit outcome for both models on identical candidates. Estimate the macro difference as the average of four category differences; bootstrap paired users within each category, recomputing that macro difference each time. [Paired binary comparison methods](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/DTComPair/html/dtcompair-package.html) support McNemar tests based on discordant outcomes. With 200 users/category, one changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and the macro score by 0.00125. Such intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and fixed candidates; they do not correct adaptive selection or measure training-seed variability. [Krichene and Rendle](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/651) show sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model rankings, so conclusions must remain specific to the pinned sampled protocol.

For augmentation comparisons, the methodological implication is equal total GPU-second budgets, counting tuning, preprocessing on GPU, diagnostics and failed trials; equal trial counts can favor expensive methods. Use matching hardware, seeds, evaluator and stopping policies, and include augmentation-off ablations. [Dacrema et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.07698) identify inadequate baseline optimization as a source of misleading progress. Report per-category results alongside macro HR and best-so-far performance versus consumed compute.
